identification: Three Tasmanian pottery pieces from the Campbell Pottery, Launceston: (1) small ribbed beehive vase in green/blue drip glaze, incised 'B553 John Campbell Tasmania' (John Campbell, Launceston, c.1930s-50s); (2) larger ovoid green-glazed vase with flared collar, unmarked on base (photographed), has a glaze chip/flake at foot rim, glaze and form consistent with Campbell but unattributed; (3) blue-glazed dish shaped as a map of Tasmania, inscribed 'Launceston Tas.' with base 'By Rupert Campbell Launceston Tas' (hand-signed by Rupert Campbell, John's son). Armitage estimate 50-70, current bid $15, AS IS.

viewing_check: Armitage estimate 50-70, current bid $15 (+22% premium). John Campbell (Launceston) is the sought-after Tasmanian pottery; the B553 ribbed vase is signed and typically sells A$40-60 on eBay; the Tasmania-shaped dish hand-signed Rupert Campbell is worth A$70-115; the big green vase is unmarked, so inspect the base for a Campbell mark, the foot chip and any repair, and check the size (photos give no scale). Estimated eBay resale if sold separately: about A$40-60 + A$70-100 + A$40-80 = A$150-240 before fees and postage. eBay prices 2024-2026 are fairly steady, with more sales recently (about 4 a month in Terapeak). Older auction prices (2017-2024) are higher for early dated or large pieces.
